title: Clarify drawImage(<svg preserveAspectRatio>)

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body: There is currently an interop issue when drawing an SVG image to a canvas regarding the scaling operation. Let `source_image` be a detached HTMLImageElement with no `width` nor `height` attributes pointing to an SVG document whose root <svg> element has `` element as *image*, which would be against what [*CanvasImageSource*](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts) says. So in this exact case, they'll stretch it like Chrome but with all the antialias artifacts, and if the `` has a width and height on its own (even if set only through CSS) they'll pass what's rendered in that `` to `drawImage()`. [[fiddle]](https://jsfiddle.net/kytz02pr/). If we try to find what the specs have to say, we have in [`drawImage`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#drawing-images) > Paint the region of the *image* argument specified by the source rectangle on the region of the rendering context's output bitmap specified by the destination rectangle, after applying the current transformation matrix to the destination rectangle. Both interpretations sound possible here. We need to check what *image* really means and in what state it is: if it doesn't have a size yet, SVG's [`viewBox`](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/coords.html#ViewBoxAttribute) and [`preserveAspectRatio`](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/coords.html#PreserveAspectRatioAttribute) probably can't be used and the SVG doesn't have a viewport, which means it's in an undefined state. Trying to go back to what is this "*image* argument" leads to [CanvasImageSource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts) which states > When a *CanvasImageSource* object represents an *HTMLOrSVGImageElement*, the element's image must be used as the source image. And then going to [HTMLImageElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#htmlimageelement), there doesn't seem to be anything specifying in which state is an "*image*" representing a vector graphic, so it's hard to tell who's right. FWIW, as a web-author I was assuming Firefox's behavior was the correct one because it made sense to me to have the *dest_rect* act as the final host for the SVG image, but that was before I read the `drawImage` specs... Now I just don't know anymore. ____ 1. Actually Chrome doesn't seem to really use the *intrinsic size*, as can be seen when [drawing an image without intrinsic width and height](https://jsfiddle.net/7dutgLkr/), but in our easy-on-purpose example it comes to the same result.
